punchline: A 1974 geometry paper by Simons and Chern ended up in physics.
thirty_sec: At Stony Brook Simons wrote a pure-geometry paper with Shiing-Shen Chern, published in the Annals of Mathematics in 1974. Years later Edward Witten used what became Chern-Simons theory to compute knot invariants, and it spread into string theory.
question: What small piece of work in your own field are you doing only because it is good, with no use in mind yet?
key_contrast: The paper was judged on soundness first; the physics found it later.
